items.answerKey: A clear ethanol extract becomes milky when added to water
candidateChoices: Iodine changes from brown to blue-black
Heated Benedict’s produces a brick-red precipitate
Biuret changes from blue to lilac

items.sourceConcept: purple Biuret is a positive test for protein
items.stem: Biuret reagent turns purple in a food extract. Which nutrient has been detected?
items.answerKey: Protein
candidateChoices: Lipid
Protein
Starch
Reducing sugar

items.sourceConcept: no cloudy emulsion means lipid was not detected

items.answerKey: Lipid was not detected
candidateChoices: Lipid was not detected
Protein was not detected
Lipid was detected
Starch was not detected

items.answerKey: Reducing sugar was not detected under these conditions
candidateChoices: Reducing sugar was not detected under these conditions
The drink must contain starch
The drink contains no sweet-tasting substances

items.answerKey: A sweet substance need not be a reducing sugar
candidateChoices: Sweetness shows that the drink contains protein

items.sourceConcept: Biuret reagent is required to test for protein

items.answerKey: Biuret reagent

Benedict’s solution
Ethanol
Iodine solution

items.sourceConcept: the control suggests contamination or a problem with reagents
items.stem: The water blank and food sample both become milky in an emulsion test. Why is the sample result uncertain?
items.answerKey: The blank shows that the procedure or materials can produce cloudiness without the food
candidateChoices: The blank shows that the procedure or materials can produce cloudiness without the food
The blank confirms lipid came specifically from the food
The blank measures the mass of lipid in the food
The blank confirms that the food contains protein

items.sourceConcept: repeat using fresh clean equipment and reagents
items.stem: How should a pupil investigate a cloudy emulsion-test blank?
items.answerKey: Repeat the blank and sample with clean equipment and fresh materials
candidateChoices: Keep the same blank and count the sample as positive
Use the sample as its own negative control
Replace the blank with oil and use it as a negative control
Repeat the blank and sample with clean equipment and fresh materials

items.sourceConcept: iodine starch testing does not require heating

items.answerKey: Room temperature
candidateChoices: After cooling the mixture to freezing
Just below boiling in a hot-water bath
Room temperature
While warming the sample over a burner

items.sourceConcept: add iodine solution to the sample and observe whether it turns blue-black
items.stem: Which method and observation would support starch in an unknown food?
items.answerKey: Add iodine solution and look for blue-black
candidateChoices: Add iodine solution and look for lilac
Add iodine solution and look for blue-black
Heat with Benedict’s and look for green
Mix with Biuret reagent and look for blue

items.answerKey: It can ignite
candidateChoices: It can condense into liquid droplets on a cool surface
It can ignite
It can carry some dissolved ethanol away from an open container
It can become more dilute when mixed with surrounding air

items.answerKey: The vapour can catch fire
candidateChoices: The vapour can catch fire
A yellow safety flame cannot ignite ethanol vapour
Ethanol can ignite only if it is heated to boiling first
